- Can you confirm the tokens/session you assumed for the "intake + 3 follow-ups" flow (avg and 90th pct)?
- What warm KV cache hit-rate did you model for the Acme pilot traffic (and what should we expect in production after prefetch warm-up)?

Alex — thanks for the note. Quick response and attaching a short packet with the numbers and sim results (see attachments). High level:

Attachment stubs: prefetched-sim-results.xlsx (spreadsheet), acme_map_draft_v2.pdf (MAP with timeline), tokens-per-conversation-scenario.csv (scenario exports)

Summary (short):
- Baseline conversation model: intake ~ 120 tokens, each follow-up ~ 80 tokens. So avg (intake + 3 follow-ups) = 360 tokens/session. 90th pct assumed at ~620 tokens/session (longer follow-ups + extra clarifying Qs).
- Tokens/$ calibration used the dedicated-optimized model profile we discussed (approx 22k tokens per USD at current quantized runtime profile for 4096 context). That maps to ~0.016 USD/session on avg in the baseline sim (see spreadsheet).
- Warm KV cache hit-rate: we modeled a 65% steady-state prefix hit-rate after a 24–48 hour warm-up in the pilot. Prefetching the top 20% of common prefixes (per route) pushed simulated steady-state to ~78% in our traffic sample.
- Batching thresholds: we recommend conservative per-request concurrency target of 6 requests/batch for the first month (low-latency tier); with 12+ requests/batch you get much better tokens/$ but latency tail increases ~30–50ms.

Planned asks: Ben, can you validate the tokens/$ conversion I'm using? Rachel, please confirm the timeline language in the MAP appendix (we need the procurement milestones to reflect the warm-up window).

If this looks ok I can update the MAP and re-run the cost appendix for their procurement team.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead — Redwood Inference

Adding some technical validation on the cache and batching assumptions — copying the relevant lines from Sofia and Ben for reference.

Key points:
- Warm KV cache hit-rate: 65% baseline after 24–48h is reasonable for a pilot if you prefetch the most common patient-intent prefixes and keep a small LRU per-worker. The 78% number is achievable but sensitive to per-route entropy (if Acme has many unique patient prompts the effective hit-rate drops). Expect 8–12% variance across routes.

- Prefetch strategy: prefetch top-N prefixes for the 10 most frequent routes during idle windows; + async background refresh every 10 minutes. That gives good steady-state without increasing tail latency.

- Batching vs latency: empirical numbers from bench:
  - single-request latency (p50) on dedicated-optimized = 22ms/token initial, p95 add ~120ms due to scheduling.
  - batching 6 reqs -> amortized kernel overhead reduces per-token cost by ~18%.
  - batching 12 reqs -> additional ~12% cost reduction vs 6 but p95 latency increases by ~30–45ms (depends on queueing).

- Tokens/session calc sanity check (quick):
  - avg path: 120 + 3*80 = 360 tokens -> at 20k tokens/USD -> 0.018 USD/session.
  - 90th path: 620 tokens -> 0.031 USD/session.

Operational recommendation to include in MAP:
1) Use the conservative tokens/USD (20k) for procurement appendix; include optimistic column (22k) as an alternative.
2) Call out warm-up window (48h) as a mutual action item — Acme to provide synthetic and early traffic to accelerate prefetching.
3) Add an acceptance gate: if after 14 days steady-state cache hit-rate < 60% we trigger a joint traffic-analysis sprint and adjust pricing credits accordingly (this is a measurable MAP milestone).

Happy to put these into a one-pager we can attach to the MAP.

— Karthik
